## Room-Temperature Sensors for Breath Acetone Detection

| A. Author ∗ NIT Calicut a.author@example.com   | B. Author ∗ IIT Madras b.author@example.com   |
|------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|

## Abstract

We report a PEDOT:PSS chemiresistive sensor functionalized with gold and palladium nanoparticles that operates at room temperature with a response time under 8 seconds.

## 1 Introduction

Metal oxide sensors typically require operating temperatures above 300 C, which increases power consumption and limits portability. Room-temperature operation is therefore desirable for wearable devices.

<!-- image -->

## 2.1 Nanoparticle Synthesis

Gold nanoparticles were synthesized by reducing chloroauric acid with sodium citrate at 95 C for 30 minutes, giving an average diameter of 15 nm.

## 3 Results

The composite sensor exhibited a response time of 7.2 seconds at 5 ppm acetone, compared to 24 seconds for the undoped control.

<!-- formula-not-decoded -->

Table 1: Response time and sensitivity of the tested sensors.

| Sensor        | Response time (s)   | Detection limit (ppm)   |
|---------------|---------------------|-------------------------|
| PEDOT:PSS     | 24.0                | 1.5                     |
| PEDOT:PSS/AuPd | 7.2                | 0.5                     |

## 4 Discussion

The improved response time is attributed to enhanced charge transfer at the nanoparticle-polymer interface, and palladium appears to play a catalytic role in acetone chemisorption.
